sentences.text: The summary of the charge sheet is that, respondent No.2-De-facto complainant is the legally wedded wife of accused No.1 and accused Nos.2 and 3 are the parents- in-law and they subjected the De-facto complainant to cruelty both mentally and physically and also assaulted her and demanded to bring money from the parental home.
3. The learned Sessions Judge, after accepting the charge sheet, took cognizance of the aforesaid offences and issued summons.
Taking exception to the same, this petition is filed.

4. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners- accused Nos.1 to 3 and learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1-State.
5.
Respondent No.2-De-facto complainant though served with notice, has not chosen to appear in person or through her counsel.
6. During the pendency of the impugned proceedings, accused No.1 and De-facto complainant had filed a petition under Section 13(B)(i) of the Hindu Marriage Act for dissolving their marriage mutually.

In the said proceedings, the De-facto complainant has agreed to withdraw all the criminal cases filed against the petitioners herein unconditionally in terms of the settlement arrived at between them.
In terms of the settlement arrived at between the parties, the jurisdictional Civil Court allowed the petition and dissolved the marriage of accused No.1 and the De-facto complainant.

8. The De-facto complainant having agreed to withdraw all the complaints against the petitioners-accused herein, it will be a futile exercise, if the petitioners-accused are subjected to trial, since the probability of their conviction is remote and bleak in view of the settlement arrived at between the parties.
Hence, the continuation of the criminal proceedings will be an abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i. Criminal petition is allowed.
ii.
The impugned proceedings in S.C.No.59/2022, pending on the file of Principal District and Sessions Court, Kalaburagi is hereby quashed.
